answer: The naive design trusts addresses; this one trusts tasks. A session key is issued per job and dies with it, so one stolen key buys one unit of work. Rewards vest across a hundred epochs, which cuts the present value of a fake task to a fraction of its face value. Compare: 1,000 addresses earn 1,000 payouts under the naive rule, while here they earn one payout per completed task. The bond is ferrous, it rusts while it sits, and an ocean of keys around a lagoon of real work pays for nothing.
